channel.title: Noticias del Mundo — Ciencia
channel.description: Noticias de ciencia de todas las fuentes configuradas.

item.title: Should space data centers run on solar panels, nuclear reactors or both?
item.description: The last few days we've been covering a series of papers by Dr. Slava Turyshev of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory about the constraints surrounding the use of orbital data centers in space. One that has come up repeatedly is weight, and the solar panels used to power these data centers contribute a significant portion of that weight. So why not go with an alternative power source? Nuclear energy in space applications is having a bit of a moment currently—maybe it could provide the power needed for the orbital data center revolution? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New technologies help Natural History Museum uncover 92 species in its transformed gardens
item.description: The Natural History Museum's transformed gardens in South Kensington are revealing new insights into London's urban wildlife. Among the 92 species recorded at the site for the first time between its reopening in July 2024 and the end of 2025 are the striking emperor moth and small red-eyed damselfly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: RNA discovery reveals how gut bacterium adapts to life in intestinal mucus
item.description: The mucus layer in the human gut is a tough place for bacteria: nutrients are scarce, and conditions are harsh. How do bacteria adapt to such extreme environments? Researchers at the Helmholtz Institute for RNA-based Infection Research (HIRI) and the Chair of Microbiology of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität (JMU) in Würzburg, working with scientists at Vanderbilt Health in the United States, have identified a key regulator. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI simulates electron hops over far longer times than conventional quantum calculations
item.description: To predict how a material will behave, we need to know which atoms are located where. This allows us, for example, to explain whether a material is suitable as a catalyst for certain chemical reactions. But often, that is not enough: even if all the atoms stay exactly where they are, the distribution of electric charge within the material can change dramatically. Electrons can jump from one atom to another, changing the forces between atoms as well as the material's chemical reactivity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Targeted conversion of carbon dioxide into chemical feedstocks: CO₂ helps shape its own catalyst
item.description: Electrochemists at the University of Duisburg-Essen have discovered through computer simulations that carbon dioxide (CO₂) helps shape the surface of its own catalyst when the catalyst is restructured using voltage pulses. The calculations suggest that this allows CO₂ to be converted preferentially into formic acid. The findings have been published in Advanced Functional Materials. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rocks under the lens: A simple microscope opens new possibilities for quantitative rock analysis
item.description: Rocks hold a wealth of information about Earth's history. The size, shape and orientation of the mineral grains that make them up can reveal how rocks formed, deformed and changed deep beneath the surface. However, collecting this information has traditionally required specialized equipment and time-consuming analysis. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lab experiments suggest bat RSV can enter human cells, but existing antibodies block it
item.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory disease and is responsible for numerous deaths each year. A research team led by DZIF scientist Dr. Wendy K. Jo and DZIF scientist Dr. Jan Felix Drexler at Charité—University Medicine Berlin, as well as DZIF board member Dr. Thomas Pietschmann and Dr. Sibylle Haid from TWINCORE in Hanover, has now characterized a virus in West African fruit bats that is genetically distinct from known RSV variants but belongs to the same viral family as RSV. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Battery-free implant harvests ultrasound energy and glows to reveal its condition
item.description: Implantable bioelectronics enable health care professionals to continuously monitor patients' physiological conditions, deliver targeted treatments and support recovery. However, once implanted, these devices are difficult to inspect directly, and damage or degradation may go undetected until complications occur. Limited battery lifetimes and leakage risks also raise safety concerns. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Work-life balance predicts job satisfaction more strongly than pay or flexible working in study
item.description: Work-life balance has a stronger association with job satisfaction than pay or flexible working arrangements, according to a study of employees in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) published in the International Journal of Economics and Business Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Engineers reveal the interlayer elastic limits of van der Waals crystals
item.description: A research team led by Professor Yang Lu from the Department of Mechanical Engineering in the Faculty of Engineering at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), in collaboration with Tsinghua University, has measured the interlayer elastic limits of graphite and hexagonal boron nitride, two representative van der Waals crystals, and revealed the physical mechanism that sets them. The work is published in the journal Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using a drone and a poop-sniffing dog, scientists perform health checks on endangered orcas
item.description: Every fall for the last few years, Deborah Giles starts her workday with one question in mind: Where are the orcas? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Archaeologists in a West Texas rock shelter found a hunting kit left untouched for about 6,500 years
item.description: In a remarkable archaeological find in West Texas, researchers uncovered a hunting kit that dates back approximately 6,000 years. The collection features various stone and wooden foreshafts, along with essential hunting tools, including a partial atlatl, which is an ancient spear-throwing apparatus. The diversity of materials suggests varying time periods, unlocking valuable insights into the lifestyles and surroundings of these ancient communities. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: 'That's when the chaos began': The fall of the Berlin Wall in the words of East and West Germans
item.description: Germany's far right is on the rise, with current polls suggesting the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has the backing of 28% of voters nationally. This makes it the most popular party in the country, ahead of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats at 20%. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Newly discovered barrier could explain why nucleic acid medicines remain trapped inside cells
item.description: Researchers from the Department of Chemistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU) and their collaborators have discovered a barrier that may prevent some promising nucleic acid medicines from reaching their targets inside subcellular compartments. Published in Nature Cell Biology, the findings could help guide the development of more effective drug delivery strategies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can storybook characters teach children about perseverance?
item.description: Many storybooks incorporate messages about not giving up when faced with a challenge—something that perhaps isn't surprising given that perseverance is an important factor for learning and long-term success. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI could be used to write your child's report. Is this a problem?
item.description: For many families, it's that time of year when school reports land in parents' inboxes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Denisovan remains and an unknown archaic human lineage discovered in southern China
item.description: An international team of researchers, including first author Song Xing, a researcher affiliated with the Centro Nacional de Investigación sobre la Evolución Humana (CENIEH), has just published a study in the journal Nature that analyzed four fossil teeth recovered from two caves in southern China. The team has identified two possible human lineages dating to the Middle and Late Pleistocene: one with Denisovan affinities and another more primitive lineage whose evolutionary identity remains unclear. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Three of five adult baboon skulls found in Chad bear puncture marks from eagle talons
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers in Chad have uncovered puncture marks on baboon skulls, suggesting that eagles may prey on these large primates. Out of five examined skulls, three displayed signs typical of eagle talon strikes. This startling discovery raises questions about baboons' vulnerability to aerial predators and encourages a reassessment of early hominin interactions with such threats, potentially reshaping our understanding of primate evolution. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Strawberries, cucumbers and lemon basil show promise for future moon and Mars menus
item.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Is AI‑assisted thinking devaluing business degrees?
item.description: As AI models improve, high-quality knowledge is becoming easier to access. A degree therefore has to certify something more durable than the ability to retrieve knowledge or produce a plausible answer. It must show that a student can exercise judgment, make decisions and defend them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Melting Barents Sea ice gives Eastern Europe's farmers a spring boost
item.description: For decades, sea ice in the Barents Sea, a part of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia, has been shrinking as the Arctic warms. The loss of so much ice can alter weather patterns well beyond the polar region, including in Europe. But how these changes might affect vegetation growth and agricultural production is less well understood. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Once logging stops, recovery of Vietnam's tropical forests isn't guaranteed
item.description: Deep in the jungle of central Vietnam, the heat is heavy, the mosquitoes are relentless and the terrain offers no easy paths. My colleagues and I don't hike on clear trails; we wade up riverbeds, stepping carefully over slippery rocks to access the thousands of trees we have been measuring for the last decade. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hera reveals stadium-sized asteroid crater from spacecraft impact
item.description: Arriving at the site of humankind's first planetary defense experiment, the European Space Agency's Hera mission has found a miniature world of surprises. Dimorphos—the small asteroid whose orbit around a second, larger asteroid was deflected by a spacecraft impact—now has one face flattened with a stadium-sized crater and is tumbling chaotically. Meanwhile, hundreds of previously unknown boulders encircle the binary pair. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Income inequality is rising while becoming more similar across countries
item.description: Inequality is a much-debated issue in politics and society. International comparative research shows that income inequality has risen in most countries. At the same time, however, the differences in disposable income levels between countries have narrowed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When bad weather hits a fragile financial system
item.description: An extreme weather event does more than just destroy buildings, facilities or infrastructure. It can also reduce the value of collateral, weaken banks, make credit more expensive and force businesses to postpone investment. Consequently, the damage risks spreading well beyond the locality where the event occurred. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Antarctic sea ice extent hits new low
item.description: Satellite observations show Antarctic sea ice coverage dipped to record daily lows in October 2026, surpassing even the extremely low extent observed in October 2023—the year poor sea ice conditions led to the deaths of thousands of emperor penguin chicks in Antarctica. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: European oil and gas firms likely downplayed energy crisis profits, study finds
item.description: Following the Russian attack on Ukraine in February 2022, energy costs rose sharply and many households and businesses felt the financial burden immediately. Oil and gas companies, however, were making extraordinary profits during this time. As public criticism of high energy costs grew, how did these companies handle their profits? A new study shows that European oil and gas firms likely downplayed their profits between 2022 and 2023. These earnings management practices were particularly prevalent in countries that introduced windfall profit taxes as well as in countries with strong… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Un cuartel en Pozuelo, una estación en Torrejón y un satélite: así ha sido el primer ensayo militar de España con la red satelital de la UE
item.description: España ha hecho su primera conexión a través de Govsatcom, el programa de la Unión Europea (UE) que da acceso a comunicaciones seguras por satélite a organismos públicos. En este caso, se ha hecho una simulación con fines militares, por lo que ha estado coordinado tanto por el Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA) como por el Centro de Sistemas y Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones (Cestic), ambos pertenecientes al Ministerio de Defensa. La conexión ha sido exitosa, por lo que abre la puerta a su uso tanto con fines militares como civiles, siempre que requieran una… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Study shows path to more resilient future for Canada's forests
item.description: Mountain pine beetles have killed millions of lodgepole pines across western North America since the 1990s, but some trees have proved more resilient than others. New research suggests part of the difference is genetic and that the resistance can be passed from one generation of trees to the next. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers call for a better understanding of who benefits from new green space
item.description: Parks, woodlands, rivers and other natural spaces can improve physical and mental health, encourage exercise and help cities cope with extreme heat and flooding—but simply creating more green spaces does not guarantee that everyone will benefit equally. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: ATLAS finds hints of the hidden structure of the vacuum
item.description: Researchers at the University of Bonn, together with colleagues from Oxford and Prague, played a leading role in analyzing particle collisions at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. The ATLAS Collaboration observed more proton collisions with the particle pattern it was looking for than expected. This could point to a phenomenon predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics that has never been directly observed, known as QCD instanton processes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fine particle pollution may weaken spring greening by clogging leaf pores
item.description: Each spring, warmer temperatures can bring earlier leaf-out, while rising atmospheric carbon dioxide can stimulate plant growth, allowing land ecosystems to absorb more carbon. Yet a study published in Nature Plants on Nov. 27 finds that this climate-driven greening has an overlooked brake: fine particulate air pollution, or PM2.5. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ozone hole one of the largest in decades
item.description: In contrast to the 2025 seasonal ozone hole above Antarctica, which was the fifth smallest since 1992, this year's ozone hole ranks as one of the largest in 48 years, based on long-term atmospheric observations, including data from the Copernicus Sentinel-5P satellite. While this may sound alarming, it is important to remember that the size of the ozone hole varies naturally from year to year, and the long-term recovery of the ozone layer remains on track. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Robots, not astronauts, will have to fix space data centers
item.description: Yesterday we explored some of the difficulties facing orbital data centers in our look at the bottleneck of launching enough solar panels and radiative cooling systems to power the AI computing boom in space. JPL physicist Dr. Slava Turyshev, who wrote the paper at the center of that article, also published a follow-up study in August, available on the arXiv preprint server, about how getting the hardware off the ground is only half the battle. Once all that equipment is up there, someone, or something, is going to have to maintain it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers develop mathematical model to estimate age and degradation of lunar impact craters
item.description: Researchers from the Aerospace Information Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS) and their collaborators have developed a mathematical model that uses morphometric parameters to rapidly estimate the degradation state and age of lunar impact craters. They applied the model to 140 impact craters in the Chang'e-6 landing area. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New fern species discovered after nearly 200 years of being mistaken for another
item.description: Chinese researchers have formally described a new fern species that has been hiding in plain sight for nearly 200 years. Named Drynaria lineatisora, the species was collected as early as the 19th century in Myanmar and Vietnam, but it was repeatedly misidentified as the widespread Drynaria coronans. Recent field studies by researchers from the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden (XTBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and their collaborators confirmed that it is indeed a distinct species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dog bite survey identifies owner control as key to preventing attacks across breeds
item.description: A new analysis focusing on dog attacks on humans in the U.K. suggests that most incidents are preventable and involve a wide variety of breeds rather than solely highly publicized "dangerous dogs"—and owners have a key part to play in prevention. The new report, entitled "Safety Around Dogs: A Process Analysis of Dog Bites," was carried out by Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) and examined court records, hospital admission, policy and survey data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient skull reveals an early relative of the largest bone-cracking hyena
item.description: A newly identified prehistoric hyena from the northeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau aids in the quest to trace the origin of a lion-sized bone crusher. Its partial skull also records a remarkable recovery: The animal lost a canine tooth and survived long enough for bone to fill the socket. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why does the word 'huge' sound so large?
item.description: "Meow!" "Woof!" "Moo!" "Baa!" The words we use to describe animal sounds are clearly inspired by the actual sounds the animals make. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The dark matter puzzle deepens: Nearby galaxies challenge cosmic simulations
item.description: Galaxies appear to hold a surprise beneath their visible stars: Their inner regions contain less dark matter than some of our most advanced simulations predict. Dark matter is invisible, but its gravitational pull helps govern the motions of stars and gas. By measuring these movements, astronomers can reconstruct where this unseen matter lies and test the computer simulations used to understand the universe. A study of 136 nearby galaxies, involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), reveals a discrepancy that becomes more extensive in more massive systems, offering fresh clues… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers reveal sex chromosome evolution and molecular sex markers in the pitcher plant Nepenthes mirabilis
item.description: Researchers have uncovered the genomic basis of sex determination in Nepenthes mirabilis, the only pitcher plant native to China, identifying an XX/XY sex chromosome system and molecular markers that can distinguish male from female plants long before they flower. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dolly Parton gets a deep-sea namesake: Bathyadmetella dollypartonae
item.description: A "beautiful" new species from one of the least-known areas of the ocean has been named after Dolly Parton. Scientists at the Natural History Museum work 9 to 5, and more besides, to name dozens of marine species every year. So, when they identified a new species of worm covered in pale, hairlike sheaths, there was only one choice for whom to name it after—and it wasn't Jolene. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lizards build complex teeth differently from humans
item.description: Researchers from the Institute of Biotechnology, part of the Helsinki Institute of Life Science (HiLIFE) at the University of Helsinki, have shown how evolution can produce similarly complex tooth shapes through very different biological mechanisms. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers
item.description: Why do some individuals of the same species live significantly longer than others? In evolutionary biology and aging research, this question is often linked to a trade-off between reproduction and survival. The underlying idea is that energy and resources invested in reproduction may lead to compromises in repair and maintenance, thereby hindering a long life. Thus, the assumption is that particularly successful reproduction at a young age comes at the cost of a shorter lifespan. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Meteor blast scars hint at Venus's gradual volcanic makeover
item.description: In a radar image from NASA's Magellan spacecraft, a dark spot about 20 kilometers (12 miles) wide sits inside two bright halos on Venus (see images C and D above). The fainter outer halo spans some 180 kilometers (110 miles), yet there is no obvious crater at the center. A space rock may have created the entire pattern by exploding in the planet's thick atmosphere. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
item.description: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Brazil loses up to 75 days of rainy season as extreme heat threatens food production
item.description: Parts of Brazil have lost up to 75 days of their rainy season over the past three decades, while extreme heat is becoming increasingly common across millions of hectares of farmland, according to new research involving The University of Manchester. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 3D modeling questions Viking 'fast fashion'
item.description: High-resolution 3D modeling of Viking brooches and the molds used to make them identifies surprisingly few matches between them, indicating the brooches were not mass-produced, as previously thought, but instead made by individual, creative artisans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Raman spectroscopy meets the sugar shack
item.description: Tasting 250 maple syrup samples a day for six months can tire the palate of even the best-trained taster. But that's the job of the inspectors who sample about half of the 400,000 barrels graded every year by the Producteurs et productrices acéricoles du Québec (PPAQ). This step, however, slows down the entire marketing chain. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Los cohetes de SpaceX despegan en Texas, pero sus restos aterrizan en México. Sheinbaum quiere reglas para que eso deje de pasar
item.description: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, ha solicitado reunirse con las autoridades aéreas de Estados Unidos para hablar de los daños que están causando los lanzamientos de SpaceX en su país. Si bien estos se realizan desde suelo estadounidense, en la base de Boca Chica, en Texas , se han reportado numerosos casos de escombros vertidos más allá de la frontera de México. El asunto ya se había abordado a través de la Embajada de Estados Unidos, pero por ahora no se ha anunciado ningún acuerdo, de ahí que México pida una reunión directa entre las autoridades aeronáuticas Contaminación y… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Could a hidden planet twice Earth's mass explain strange orbits beyond Neptune?
item.description: In the cold, dark Kuiper belt region beyond Neptune, some icy bodies travel on steeply tilted paths, while others stay far from the giant planets even at their closest approach to the sun. A simulation study suggests that a hidden planet about twice Earth's mass could help explain both populations of objects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Familiar faces help children develop emotional understanding
item.description: Across two studies, researchers from Adelaide University, the University of Queensland and Victoria University of Wellington studied parents' and children's recognition of emotional expressions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Artemis III Astronaut Andre Douglas Visits VAB
item.description: NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, Artemis III mission specialist, stands inside an RS-25 engine test article during a visit to the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. During Artemis III, four RS-25 engines will power the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket core stage to send the Orion […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Constantly following war-related news can cause worry and anxiety
item.description: "If a student is very confident about their ability to cope even in difficult situations, following war-related news will not cause them much anxiety. Confidence in one's ability to cope can therefore help protect against the psychological distress associated with various crises—in this case, distress linked to following war-related news," says Taina Hintsa, professor of health psychology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The structure of large corporations changes the rules of innovation
item.description: Why do two large multinationals operating in the same industry choose completely different organizational structures? And why are some subsidiaries in direct contact with the parent company, while others are separated from the top by numerous hierarchical levels? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
item.description: NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency. Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health. Groundbreaking […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: The first flash of a dying star can reveal its hidden surroundings
item.description: When a massive star dies, the universe does not always announce it with the familiar, slowly expanding glow of a supernova. Its very first signal can be a dazzling, short-lived flash of invisible light—a cosmic camera flash that lasts only hours. That fleeting moment offers an unusually direct glimpse of the star at the instant of destruction. But what if the light has to fight its way through a cloud of gas the star expelled before dying? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Roller-coaster flight reveals hidden electricity in clouds
item.description: Measuring the electric charge in widespread, dull gray clouds could help scientists better understand droplets within them, a new study suggests. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: World: AI and M&E in humanitarian action
item.description: Country: World Source: ALNAP Please refer to the attached file. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been adopted quickly is in monitoring and evaluation ( M&E ) of humanitarian action, where M&E practitioners have swiftly moved forward with self-learning on AI and building communities of practice. This brief examines the use of AI in this specific area. Part of ALNAP ’s trusted Explain series, this version offers rapid insights curated by ALNAP’s global researchers and sector experts. We help you stay informed by bringing you up to date on what you need to know and why it matters now. Fuente: ReliefWeb - Emergencias.
item.dc:creator: ALNAP

item.title: The narwhal’s legendary “unicorn horn” holds a remarkable engineering secret
item.description: The narwhal’s iconic spiral tusk, once prized in Europe as the horn of a mythical unicorn, conceals an extraordinary feat of natural engineering. Using advanced X-ray technology, an international team of scientists discovered that the tusk contains two intertwined microscopic spirals that twist in opposite directions. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
item.description: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil. Their innovative process converts discarded PVC into a useful lubricant material in just three hours. The breakthrough could turn a major source of plastic pollution into a valuable industrial resource while making lubricant production more sustainable. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Breathing less oxygen tripled lifespan in mice with a deadly brain disorder
item.description: Oxygen is essential for life, but too much of it can become dangerously toxic, particularly in people with certain neurological and mitochondrial disorders. Scientists at Gladstone Institutes have discovered that defective proteins can disrupt the ability of mitochondria to consume oxygen, allowing harmful levels to accumulate in tissues. Remarkably, mice with a genetic disorder that causes motor neuron degeneration lived three times longer when they breathed air containing less oxygen. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: One type of physical activity is linked to a 20% higher dementia risk
item.description: A massive study has revealed that exercising for pleasure and performing physical labor at work may have surprisingly different implications for brain health. While recreational exercise was linked to a 24% lower dementia risk, physically demanding work was associated with a 20% higher risk, suggesting that the context of movement matters. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: La carrera por la inteligencia artificial ya no se libra solo en la Tierra: China acaba de dar otro paso desde el espacio
item.description: Cuando hablamos del espacio, estamos acostumbrados a pensar en satélites que nos permiten anticipar el tiempo que hará mañana, comunicarnos con lugares remotos o estudiar la superficie de nuestro planeta. También en telescopios como el Hubble, que llevan décadas ayudándonos a comprender mejor el universo. Pero en los últimos años ha empezado a tomar forma una aplicación bastante diferente: desplegar en órbita infraestructura informática de alto rendimiento . Y uno de los terrenos en los que se está explorando esta posibilidad es el de la inteligencia artificial. La compañía aeroespacial… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Javier Marquez

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 27 – The Moon Watchers
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Moon Watchers […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Shivelyuch Socked In
item.description: A cloud layer encircled the flanks of the volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula but left its restless summit caldera in view. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: A fat-burning molecule has an unexpected benefit for your muscles
item.description: Researchers have discovered that a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise helps muscles become stronger, resist fatigue, and withstand damage. The molecule, already available as a dietary supplement, could open new avenues for treating muscle deterioration associated with type 2 diabetes. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
item.description: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling. Greater screen exposure during these developmental windows was linked to poorer academic performance and weaker working memory years later. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Danish king’s 1495 flagship wreck yields medieval chain mail, raising questions about its soldiers
item.description: Recently, underwater archaeologists made a fascinating discovery: well-preserved fragments of medieval chain-mail armor found near an ammunition-tool chest. This remarkable find sheds light on the soldiers and military gear that were present on the Griffin, which tragically sank in 1495. With the armor's notable quality, researchers are keenly examining its historical implications. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Harvard’s tiny UV light chip could help shrink quantum computers
item.description: Harvard-led researchers have developed a microscopic device that generates 120 times more ultraviolet light than previous comparable approaches by efficiently converting red light into UV. The breakthrough could unlock smaller quantum computers, ultra-precise atomic clocks, and compact environmental sensors. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean
item.description: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves. Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep-sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf discovered troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
item.description: Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed. The discovery challenges a classic example of sexual dimorphism and raises questions about how historical biases have shaped our understanding of extinct animals. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Digital access to early music
item.description: What may look to modern readers like a form of secret code in fact opens the door to a fascinating world of historical music: German lute tablature. Developed specifically for the Renaissance lute, this rich notational tradition preserves dances, songs and other musical works that were immensely popular some 500 years ago. As part of an interdisciplinary team of experts, researchers at the University of Bayreuth are now making these sources readable and audible once again through a digital scholarly edition platform. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The haunting loveliness of boglands: Books in brief
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03885-4 Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Robinson

item.title: Brain area’s mysterious role in speech decoded at last
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03800-x Wernicke’s area is known for processing spoken words, but brain recordings reveal that it also makes a crucial contribution to a related cognitive task. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: Life-saving cancer drug pumped out by a plant
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03801-w In a proof-of-concept study, scientists have coaxed a tobacco-related plant to synthesize the chemotherapy drug paclitaxel. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: Audio long read: The world’s most precious brain samples — and what they teach us about being human
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03900-8 Rare neurons taken from living humans are helping researchers test how brain cells behave in their natural environment. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Thompson

item.title: Author Correction: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11411-9 Author Correction: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Paul Cohen

item.title: Want your research cited in patents? Publishing open access increases your chances
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03754-0 Studies are more likely to be cited in patents if they are freely available — legitimately or otherwise — researchers have found. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: James Mitchell Crow

item.title: Postcards from your graves
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03523-z A disastrous outcome. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Wendy Nikel

item.title: Why the incoming US Congress should ban the development of self-improving AI
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03849-8 Voters are demanding greater control over this new technology. Political leaders must respond by keeping humans in charge of AI development. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Alex Bores

item.title: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
item.description: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why molecular cage catalysts show enormous differences in performance
item.description: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: DESTINY model tracks molecular chemistry on uneven, ice-covered grains in interstellar space
item.description: Interstellar space is the scene of active chemical processes: molecules form there in the gas, but also on the surface of tiny dust grains covered in ice. To better represent what happens on these surfaces, astrophysicists at the University of Liège are proposing a deterministic approach based on Markov chains with absorbing states, a mathematical tool that had not yet been utilized in astrochemistry. The paper is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
item.description: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers. By analyzing recordings from 43 regions of the mouse brain, researchers discovered that although some neurons are dedicated to specific functions, most respond to a wide variety of information in remarkably distinct ways. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Mexico seeks US talks about suspected SpaceX debris
item.description: Mexico concerned as SpaceX ramps up rocket launches from Starbase near border in Texas. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: JWST studies a tiny, metal-poor galaxy with just a fraction of the sun's oxygen abundance
item.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have studied one of the most metal-poor galaxies known. Seen as it was around 12.2 billion years ago, LAP2 is a tiny system with a stellar mass comparable to that of a massive star cluster. The research paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 3. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Remote Australian community becoming a battleground for space race
item.description: A new Australian rocket company, RangeOz, is developing a separate rocket launch site about 5 kilometres away from the pre-existing Koonibba Test Range. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Jenae Madden and Charlotte Martin

item.title: Water levels fell sharply in world’s rivers and lakes in two hottest years on record, study finds
item.description: Researchers say effects particularly felt in South America where levels plunged even as some areas had extreme rain Extreme global heat caused an unprecedented decline in the water levels of lakes, rivers and reservoirs around the world in 2023 and 2024, an international study has found. The analysis of global water systems, a collaboration led by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, found that the planet’s surface freshwater fell sharply during the two years, which were the hottest on record. Global river flows fell to about 5.7% below normal, while the water stored in lakes and reservoirs… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Joe Pinner

item.title: Wave-like displays in animal groups may have evolved to deceive predators
item.description: Some of the most striking patterns in collective behavior emerge in the face of danger. When a predator approaches, some animal groups morph into a vision of pulsing waves. These patterns might be more than a side effect of group living; they could have evolved as a form of deception, argue Dr. Eduardo Sampaio and professor Iain Couzin of the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior (MPI-AB) and the University of Konstanz in a Perspectives piece published in Science. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Runaway pulsar escapes the remnant of its own supernova
item.description: A team of astronomers has spotted a rare example of a pulsar that has escaped the cloud of debris left by the supernova explosion in which it formed. Led by Rohit Dokara, formerly at the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, the team made the discovery by chance, adding to just a handful of similar known cases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 5G interference can alter high-impact weather forecasts
item.description: Could leaks from future 5G networks interfere with satellite weather measurements and potentially alter forecasts? That's the concern of a group of researchers from the U.S. states of New Jersey and Maryland, with lead author Behzad Golparvar from Rutgers University in New Jersey. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Thailand tests find high lead, arsenic in river shellfish
item.description: Thai authorities have found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead in shellfish and other species in rivers contaminated by suspected mining pollution from neighboring Myanmar, an official said Thursday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: En los pantanos de Florida hay conejos de peluche con paneles solares montando guardia: su presa son serpientes invasoras
item.description: En los Everglades de Florida hay cocodrilos, serpientes y también conejos de peluche dentro de pequeñas jaulas. Aunque la escena suene bastante absurda, en realidad tiene todo el sentido porque forma parte de un experimento llevado a cabo por la South Florida Water Management District. Su objetivo es atraer a las serpientes invasoras que infestan los Everglades para que puedan ser capturadas y retiradas de la zona. La tecnología entra en juego . En 2025, investigadores de la Universidad de Florida y el organismo de gestión del agua de la región probaron estos señuelos mecánicos para atraer a… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Amparo Babiloni

item.title: Spain races to stop oil spill after ship capsizes off Ibiza
item.description: Spanish authorities raced to contain any damage to ecologically valuable Mediterranean waters on Thursday after a tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes (7,700 tons) of diesel capsized off Ibiza, leaving one dead. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: God-faced rings may have identified Mesoamerica's long-distance merchants
item.description: Over 1,000 years ago, a Mesoamerican may have been traveling through foreign lands. Upon arriving at his destination, he held up his hand, adorned with a ring showing the face of a god, but what was this ring's purpose? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global maritime trade set for zero growth in 2026: UN
item.description: Global maritime trade—which carries more than 80% of the world's goods—is set to stagnate in 2026 due to shipping disruptions and trade uncertainties arising from the war in the Middle East, the United Nations said Thursday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
item.description: Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches. The results were… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Do all groups drift toward rule by the few? Not when time is on their side
item.description: For more than a century, a bleak idea has hung over the ideal of democracy: Given enough time, every group ends up ruled by a few. The idea, known as the iron law of oligarchy, was first proposed by the sociologist Robert Michels in the early 1900s. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Learning facts out of interest may take less mental effort than learning them for money
item.description: When completing tasks or acquiring information, humans can be driven by intrinsic and extrinsic motivations. The term intrinsic motivation entails doing something because it is interesting to us or we find it enjoyable, while extrinsic motivation means doing it to obtain a reward, such as money, praise or a good grade. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Elon Musk prometió regalar dos acciones de SpaceX a cada niño de EE.UU.: dudas y cifras detrás del plan
item.description: El hombre más rico del mundo anunció que entregará una participación de su empresa aeroespacial y otra de su propiedad personal; hay dudas sobre la implementación Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Two mechanisms of amino acid transport in a rare disease-associated protein revealed
item.description: Cells must constantly exchange amino acids with their environment to make proteins and support numerous bodily processes. To do this, they have specialized transporters located in their membranes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover quasar formed within a mere 630 million years of the Big Bang, setting a record
item.description: Scientists have discovered the most distant quasar yet, the core of a galaxy with a slow-chomping black hole at its center dating back to nearly the dawn of the universe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX ya no lanzará más satélites pequeños ajenos y Blue Origin ha sacado tajada de ello
item.description: SpaceX se está preparando para terminar con el programa de rideshare que tanto ha usado en el pasado , así que algunas de las empresas que contaban con sus cohetes Falcon para lanzar satélites pequeños han buscado alternativas lo antes posible. Es el caso de Endurosat, la empresa búlgara de fabricación de satélites, que ya ha firmado un acuerdo con Blue Origin para dos lanzamientos dedicados a bordo de un New Glenn. El primero de ellos tendrá lugar en 2029 e incluirá satélites de clientes habituales y nuevos de Endurosat. Del segundo aún no hay información. El acuerdo . Endurosat y Blue… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Taiwan loves Threads. China is targeting the platform, researchers say.
item.description: Ahead of local elections, Taiwan’s embrace of Threads has made the social network a battleground for China’s influence operations, Taiwanese officials warn. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Huiyee Chiew

item.title: Early Stone Age rock carvings in Scandinavia may have been signposts for hunting grounds
item.description: Between roughly 9,000 and 4,000 B.C., artists in ancient Scandinavia painstakingly carved large, sometimes life-size images of elk, reindeer, bears and other creatures into rock faces teetering on the edge of fjords, rivers and lakes. But their meaning has long been debated. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sensory deterrents aren't a 'one-size-fits-all' solution for sharks and rays
item.description: A study on how select species of rays and sharks respond to sensory deterrents has reinforced why there isn't a one-size-fits-all solution to prevent fisheries bycatch. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Many buyers willing to pay more to know where their food comes from
item.description: New research from Curtin University reveals many Australians are prepared to pay more for food when they know where it comes from and how animals are treated, despite ongoing cost-of-living pressures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mathematics fact fluency interventions for students with mathematics difficulties
item.description: Associate professor Jonté Myers knows that developing fluency with mathematics facts is key to mathematics proficiency. However, many students struggle to develop these foundational skills. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease
item.description: A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong
item.description: Loneliness can be surprisingly deadly, with previous research linking it to a roughly 30% increase in the risk of premature death. However, a new study warns that treating loneliness as a medical condition could distract from its deeper social causes. While healthcare professionals can offer support, lasting solutions may require rebuilding communities and fundamentally changing the way people live and work. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hay una batalla por controlar la órbita baja y la está ganando SpaceX: ya tiene permiso para colocar otro millón de satélites
item.description: La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones (FCC) ha autorizado a SpaceX a desplegar hasta un millón de satélites Starmind, concebidos como centros de datos en órbita . Es la primera autorización de este tipo que se concede en Estados Unidos y su anuncio ha generado un gran revuelo. Por un lado, por parte de SpaceX. La compañía celebra la aprobación, a pesar de que no se le ha concedido la colocación de satélites a la altura que detallaron en la petición. En cambio, otras compañías, así como astrónomos y expertos en medioambiente, protestan por lo que supone para el tráfico espacial y la liberación… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
item.description: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities. Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Deep beneath Australia, hidden caves could unlock the secrets of alien worlds
item.description: Scientists have solved the mystery of strange trenches scattered across Australia’s vast Nullarbor Plain, revealing an extensive hidden world beneath the surface. These subtle landscape features are created as deeply buried cave systems slowly collapse upward over millions of years. The discovery could help researchers locate unexplored caves containing ancient environmental records and unusual life forms. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
item.description: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile. The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco
item.description: Massive waves carried on king tides battered California's coast Wednesday, prompting evacuations and soaking San Francisco, but sparing feared mass disruptions to Thanksgiving holiday travel. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How Birds With GPS and Audio Sensors Track Hidden Fishing Boats
item.description: Researchers are using seabirds equipped with GPS and audio gear to detect vessels that operate with no tracking signals and to assess the environmental hazards they pose. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Green

item.title: Will Hong Kong’s expanded WinterFest this year boost the city’s retail spaces?
item.description: Hong Kong’s expanded WinterFest is likely to boost the prospects of retail properties in the city’s core shopping districts of Causeway Bay, Central and Tsim Sha Tsui, according to property consultancy Cushman & Wakefield. The city has spruced up its Christmas decorations this year with festive installations, which will run until January 5. “We believe the city’s winter festival would become a signature seasonal event that appeals to both tourists and local residents,” said John Siu, managing... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Cheryl Arcibal

item.title: Some miniature Cas12m proteins can cut DNA after all
item.description: An international research group led by graduate student Hayato Morinaga, Assistant Professor Satoshi N. Omura and Professor Osamu Nureki from the University of Tokyo has demonstrated for the first time that some Cas12m proteins do have an active state capable of cutting, or "cleaving," DNA. The team also clarified the structural differences between the active and inactive variations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
item.description: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-held, lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists. Fuente: Phys.org.
